Hill, John 

        M.A.5.6.1750 on testimonials and M.D. 5.6.1750 on testimonials signed by George Pile, London and Dr Cox, M.R.C.S.Eng., London.

        Born c. 1716 2nd son of Rev. Theophilus Hill, Peterborough. [Minister]

        Apprenticed to an apothecary and set up on his own account.  Unsuccessfully tried the theatre as a career. Applied himself to literature and published much on botany. Gained knighthood of the Swedish Order of Vasa for his ‘Vegetable System’, 1774. Engaged in much controversy. The first Linnean Flora of Britain was due to him. Goodsir, Robert Anstruther 
      M.D. 22.10.1852 by examination.
      
        Born 9.7.1823 son of John Goodsir, surgeon, Anstruther and Elizabeth Taylor. [Doctor]
      
      Studied Edinburgh University - medical student 1845-1849.
        Began life in a London banking house, but decided on medicine.
        Surgeon to a Dundee whaler 1849.
        Surgeon to ‘Lady Franklin’ 1850-1851, his brother Henry having been assistant surgeon and naturalist on Franklin’s ship ‘Erebus’.
         Went to Australia seeking gold.
         Lived in New Zealand, South Sea Islands, Siberia and Russia.
         Settled in Edinburgh c. 1885. [Doctor]
      Publications.
      An Arctic voyage to Baffin's Bay and Lancaster Sound, in search of friends with Sir John Franklin, by Robert Anstruther Goodsir. (London: John van Voorst, 1850)
      
      Died Edinburgh 17.1.1895.

        M.D. 7.5.1803 on testimonials signed by John Coakley Lettsom M.D. and Philip Elliot M.D., London.
      There is some doubt about this name. Langharne seems to be what the Senatus minute says, but the testimonial is indeterminate. P.J. Wallis and R.V. Wallis, Eighteenth Century Medics (Newcastle, 1988) gives a William Laugharne as a surgeon at Carmarthen in 1782 and there was a dynasty of Elliots who were practitioners at Laugharne, Carmarthenshire.

      M.D. 6.5.1853 by examination.
      
        Born 30.9.1831 son of Andrew Ewart, Cumberland and Catherine Armstrong Ewart.
      
      Studied Guy’s hospital.
      M.R.C.S.Eng. 1853. M.R.C.P.L. 1876. F.R.C.P.L. 1881.
      Went to India.
      Became Professor then Principal in Calcutta Medical College.
      Returned to England 1876.
      Retired 1879 to Brighton and devoted his energies to municipal affairs.
      On town council 1884 - 1905.
      Mayor 1891-1894.
      Knighted 1895. [Doctor, university professor]
      Publications.
      The poisonous snakes of India. For the use of the officials and others residing in the Indian Empire.(London: J. & A. Churchill, 1878)
      Descriptive catalogue of the pathological preparations in the museum of the Medical College, Calcutta.(London: Smith, Elder & Co., 1865)
      
      
      Died 10.1.1906.
      
      Lancet 1906 i 194D.G. Crawford, Roll of the Indian Medical Service, 1615-1930 (London, 1930) B1620Munk's Roll iv 279
